title: Android 内存评审清单：上线前、灰度中、事故后
key_conclusions: Memory review should be staged into pre-launch, canary, and post-incident gates because each stage needs different evidence.
Every memory bucket touched by a change needs an owner, a metric, and a rollback line.
Low-end devices require separate review for PSI, ZRAM, lmkd, Graphics, and peak windows.
A release candidate should not ship without repeatable scenario scripts and version/RAM-class boundaries.
shallow_points: The checklist is generic and does not include a runnable CI or dashboard integration.
It does not define numeric thresholds for every metric or RAM class.
It does not include a real filled-out review form from a production incident.
It does not automate owner assignment from traces or source paths.
discovered_connections: Day 78's T0-T5 timeline becomes the review requirement for repeatable scenario scripts.
Day 77's bucket-specific evidence commands become the pre-launch and canary gates.
Day 73's validation loop becomes the release decision model: hold, ship, pause, rollback, or hotfix.
Day 80 should summarize the whole curriculum as a knowledge map with paths from symptom to evidence to source to fix.
suggest_future_topics: Day 80 should build the final Android memory expert knowledge graph.
A future tool should generate a Memory Review report from meminfo, PSI, vmstat, zram, lmkd, and trace artifacts.
A future appendix should define RAM-class-specific threshold examples.
A future CI template should run low-end scenario scripts before release.
knowledge_gaps: Need real production data to set numeric gates for PSS, PSI, ZRAM, and lmkd.
Need dashboard and alert examples for canary monitoring.
Need automation that maps evidence buckets to module owners.
Need example filled review documents for launch, canary regression, and incident response.

Applied Day 78's timeline and validation gates by turning them into staged checklist tables and release decision gates.
Applied Day 77's evidence-command model by requiring meminfo, showmap, PSI, vmstat, zram, lmkd, and version/RAM-class checks.
Applied the standing more-diagrams-less-prose feedback by using four Mermaid diagrams, checklist tables, release gates, and a compact review template.

Added tables for stage outputs, pre-launch checks, canary metrics, incident questions, release gates, review template fields, and conclusions.
Added a reusable Markdown Memory Review template for launch, canary, and incident review.
